facts.claim: Buttondown is a newsletter platform that helps users start, grow, and monetize newsletters.
facts.excerpt: Buttondown is a newsletter platform that makes it easy to start, grow, and monetize your newsletter.

facts.claim: Buttondown supports paid subscriptions via Stripe.
facts.excerpt: It supports Markdown and rich text editing, custom domains, paid subscriptions via Stripe, automations, webhooks, and deep integrations with tools like Zapier, Discord, and RSS feeds.

facts.claim: Buttondown offers one-click concierge migration and promises to migrate a whole list within one business day.
facts.excerpt: we offerone-click concierge migration for your whole list, no matter how large it may be. Just create your account for free, contact us, and we’ll get you migrated within one business day.
facts.source_title: Buttondown — Newsletter software for people like you

facts.claim: Buttondown emphasizes strong deliverability and spam protection for business email.
facts.excerpt: Buttondown’s deliverability is among the highest in the industry, and our spam protection is best-in-class.
facts.source_title: Buttondown — Newsletter software for people like you

facts.claim: Buttondown says it is a small, independent business and prioritizes its roadmap from customer feedback.
facts.excerpt: As a small, independent business, we want Buttondown to be our life’s work. We have plans in place for the really long term. No, longer than that. Longer.

strategy.observation: Buttondown publicly emphasizes one-click concierge migration and says it can migrate a whole list within one business day.
strategy.offer_link: Because Buttondown already uses migration as a core acquisition promise, a service that helps newsletter writers move from Substack could support that motion by reducing setup friction and helping handle more migration demand.
hypotheses: They may want to increase the number of Substack writers who complete a switch to Buttondown.
They may have more migration requests than their team wants to handle manually.
They may value partners or contractors who can accelerate customer onboarding without changing the product.
strategy.angle: I noticed Buttondown makes migration a core promise and can move a whole list in a day, so I thought a focused Substack migration service might help you convert more switchers with less manual lift.
strategy.fit_reason: Buttondown already positions migration as part of its value proposition, so help for writers leaving Substack is directly adjacent and plausible as a way to increase conversions or reduce operational load. It is still an assumption that they need outside help, but the fit is strong.
